extracted.intended_audience: NLP / ML researchers and practitioners building or evaluating models for mathematical problem solving and explanation-generation
extracted.subtask_description: A dataset of competition-style mathematics problems paired with full step-by-step solutions (LaTeX + natural language) intended for training and evaluating models that generate derivations/explanations and final answers. The dataset aggregates problems from contests like AMC/AIME and annotates each example with difficulty level and subject type.

rubrics_metrics.name: problem field
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each data instance includes a 'problem' field containing the text of a competition-style math problem (example provided in the card).

rubrics_metrics.name: solution field (step-by-step)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solutions are full step-by-step derivations written in LaTeX and natural language and are intended to teach models to generate answer derivations and explanations. Example shows natural-language explanation combined with LaTeX math expressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: final answer formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: The step-by-step solution contains the final answer enclosed in LaTeX's \boxed tag.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final numeric or symbolic answer is wrapped with \boxed{...} (e.g., x=\boxed{\frac{1}{4}}) to make the ground-truth answer machine-parseable and visually explicit.

rubrics_metrics.name: level annotation (difficulty)
rubrics_metrics.description: The problem's difficulty level from 'Level 1' to 'Level 5'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Levels indicate relative difficulty where a subject's easiest problems are assigned 'Level 1' and hardest problems are 'Level 5'. Use these labels to stratify difficulty during training/evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: type annotation (subject)
rubrics_metrics.description: The subject of the problem: Algebra, Counting & Probability, Geometry, Intermediate Algebra, Number Theory, Prealgebra and Precalculus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each instance has a 'type' field specifying the mathematical domain; use this to analyze model performance by topic.

rubrics_metrics.name: source competitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Problems come from mathematics competitions, including the AMC 10, AMC 12, AIME, and more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dataset examples are drawn from established contest sources, which implies particular style, difficulty distributions, and canonical solution formats worth preserving for realism.

rubrics_metrics.name: data instance format
rubrics_metrics.description: A data instance consists of a competition math problem and its step-by-step solution written in LaTeX and natural language, plus metadata fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The example JSON instance structure shown: {'problem':..., 'level':..., 'type':..., 'solution':...}. Consumers should expect and preserve this schema.

rubrics_metrics.name: data splits and sizes
rubrics_metrics.description: Dataset splits: train: 7,500 examples; test: 5,000 examples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These splits indicate available partitions for training and evaluation; note the dataset card also reports overall size range (10K < n < 100K) and total file size (7.92 MB).

rubrics_metrics.name: supported task labels / task_categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Tagged for explanation-generation (text2text-generation) and related tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The card notes 'explanation-generation' and lists a task_categories field (with a warning that 'text2text-generation' is not in Hugging Face's official list). Use the dataset for generation/evaluation of stepwise solutions and answer derivations.

rubrics_metrics.name: license
rubrics_metrics.description: License: MIT (link to LICENSE in repository).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dataset use and redistribution are governed by the MIT license referenced at the GitHub repository link; check LICENSE for exact terms before reuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: citation / provenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Citation: Hendrycks et al., 'Measuring Mathematical Problem Solving With the MATH Dataset' (arXiv:2103.03874).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users of the dataset are expected to cite the provided arXiv paper when reporting results; dataset curators and paper authors are listed in the citation.

rubrics_metrics.name: data quality / completeness claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Each problem in MATH has a full step-by-step solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit dataset property and an implied quality expectation: entries should include complete derivations rather than only final answers, enabling models to learn multi-step reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: formatting expectations (LaTeX usage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Solutions use LaTeX for mathematical notation within natural-language explanations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect LaTeX markup in solution fields (e.g., \frac{1}{3}, \boxed{...}); preprocessing or rendering pipelines should handle LaTeX tokens appropriately.
